title: El boleto falso afuera del Foro Sol

dialogue.speaker: Paco
dialogue.spanish: ¡No manches, Mariana! El lector de códigos aquí en la puerta del Foro Sol acaba de prender en rojo con mi boleto.
dialogue.english: No way, Mariana! The barcode scanner right here at the Foro Sol gate just flashed red on my ticket.

dialogue.speaker: Mariana
dialogue.spanish: ¡No me digas eso! Pues te advertí que ese revendedor de internet se veía súper chafa, Paco.
dialogue.english: Don't tell me that! Well I warned you that online reseller looked super sketchy, Paco.

slang.example: Compré unos audífonos baratos pero salieron súper chafas.

dialogue.speaker: Paco
dialogue.spanish: Espérate, bueno, ya me puse nervioso porque me costó carísimo y me quedé sin un quinto para toda la quincena.
dialogue.english: Wait a second, well, now I'm nervous because it cost me a fortune and left me without a cent for the whole two-week pay period.

slang.actualMeaning: penniless / without a single cent left
slang.example: Después de pagar la renta me quedé sin un quinto.

dialogue.speaker: Mariana
dialogue.spanish: A ver, enséñame la pantalla de tu celular... ¡Ay, Paco, o sea, estás bien dormido!
dialogue.english: Hold on, show me your phone screen... Oh, Paco, I mean, you're half asleep!

dialogue.speaker: Paco
dialogue.spanish: ¿Por qué? ¡Ah, qué oso hice con el guardia! Estaba enseñando el código QR del estacionamiento en vez del concierto.
dialogue.english: Why? Oh, how embarrassing in front of the guard! I was showing the QR code for the parking lot instead of the concert.

slang.example: ¡Qué oso cuando me tropecé frente a toda la oficina!

dialogue.speaker: Mariana
dialogue.spanish: Mira, ya se puso en verde. ¡Córrele que la banda está por tocar la primera rola y nos toca hasta la pista!
dialogue.english: Look, it just turned green. Run now, the band is about to play their first song and our spot is all the way down on the floor!

questions.question: Why do Paco and Mariana panic when they arrive at the entrance to the Foro Sol concert venue?
options: The ticket scanner flashes red on Paco's ticket, making them fear he bought a fake ticket
Paco forgot his cell phone in the parking lot
The concert was canceled due to rain
Mariana bought tickets for the wrong date
questions.explanation: The scanner flashes red ('acaba de prender en rojo'), making them fear the online reseller sold Paco a fake ticket.

questions.question: What silly mistake does Mariana discover when she looks at Paco's phone screen?
options: He was showing the QR code for the parking lot instead of the concert ticket
His screen brightness was turned all the way down
He was showing an old movie ticket
questions.explanation: Paco realizes: 'Estaba enseñando el código QR del estacionamiento en vez del concierto.'

questions.question: Why do they have to run once the real ticket scans green?
options: The band is about to play their first song ('la primera rola') and their spot is down on the floor ('la pista')
The stadium gates are closing in one minute
It is starting to rain heavily
They need to meet their friends at the merchandise booth
questions.explanation: Mariana says: 'la banda está por tocar la primera rola y nos toca hasta la pista.'

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: What do 'súper chafa', 'sin un quinto', and '¡qué oso!' mean in Mexican slang?
options: 'Súper chafa' = sketchy/low-quality; 'sin un quinto' = penniless; 'qué oso' = how embarrassing
'Súper chafa' = polite; 'sin un quinto' = five minutes late; 'qué oso' = how lucky
'Súper chafa' = expensive; 'sin un quinto' = without a ticket; 'qué oso' = how scary
'Súper chafa' = famous; 'sin un quinto' = alone; 'qué oso' = how funny
questions.explanation: In Mexico City slang, 'chafa' is sketchy/shoddy, 'sin un quinto' is penniless, and '¡qué oso!' means 'how embarrassing!'
